RFC 3948 Section 5.1: "Because SGW will now see two possible SAs that lead to 10.1.2.3, it can become confused about where to send packets coming from Suzy's server.  Implementors MUST devise ways of preventing this from occurring." ALL THREE FINDINGS OF aa3db3ac29 ARE CLOSED. Finding 1 (configured-host clause): classifyInnerPair's isConfiguredHost forced true reddens TestRFC3948TransportPeerChosenHostBesideConfiguredTunnelRefused, TestRFC3948OrderedTransportLocalHalfNarrowedRefused and TestRFC3948OrderedTransportNarrowedToPortRefused; forced false reddens TestRFC3948OrderedTransportBesideFullTunnelServed. Finding 2 (claim atomicity): TestRFC3948ConcurrentInstallsHoldOneInnerAddress reddens under claim's locks released and retaken between check and record in 10 of 10 runs under -race (the changed-package gate's pass) and 8 of 20 without it, and under the check moved out of the critical section (admit, then lock and record) in 15 of 20 without -race; a single plain run can miss it, so the -race pass is the proof. Finding 3 (initiator wiring): with runInitiator's sa.innerSelectors assignment removed, TestRFC3948InitiatorSessionRefusesHeldInnerAddress, which now waits for the Child SA or the registry-refusal Warn, is red in 30 of 30 runs at -cpu=4. RE-PROBED, each red on a tagged unit: conflictLocked overlap never true (25 units) and always true (DistinctInnerAddressesServed); claim check skipped (5, install backstop and initiator install); conflict and stranded refusal turned to continue; bothTransport true (6); priority ignored (ConfiguredOverlapEqualPriority, OrderedTransportEqualPriority); p and h operatorFixed ignored (6 and 4); samePolicyPair protocol, remote port and remote prefix each dropped; every configured selector fixing any pair; configuredHostPair local half taken from the remote address; isConfiguredHost reduced to the remote prefix, or remote prefix and port; narrowing filter off; guard registry nil, and nil for transport Child SAs; startPeerSession, tryResponderSAInit, runInitiator, applyIKERekeyResponse, respondIKERekey registry dropped; newRekeyedChild innerGuard dropped; releaseInnerRecord releasing a stranded record; lease, substitution, rekey proposal and answerNamesOnlyLeases guards off. Every tunnel-mode path probed is covered: responder IKE_AUTH, initiator IKE_AUTH, CREATE_CHILD_SA as either side, Child SA rekey either side, IKE SA rekey either side, pool-bound peers, tunnel against transport in both orders, stranded records, and concurrent installs. WHY ENFORCED DESPITE THREE UNPROVEN GUARDS: each of these breaks leaves the whole engine package green, and a scratch test at HEAD shows each is reachable, but each admits only an overlap of two pairs that both lie inside what the two operators wrote (a configured selector or the configured local and remote addresses) at policy-priority values they set apart, which the SPD orders, so no packet meets two candidate SAs unordered and no peer can claim an address the operator did not give it: (a) classifyInnerPair's `if p.transport()` widened to tunnels lets tunnel peer c (remote 198.18.0.11, no selector, priority 1000) proposing TSi 198.18.0.11/32 TSr 192.0.2.1/32 sit beside configured full tunnel a at 2000; (b) samePolicyPair's local-port test dropped lets peer b (configured remote 10.1.2.0/24 TCP, priority 1500) narrowed to local port 80 sit beside a's configured 10.1.0.0/16 at 2000; (c) its local-prefix test dropped lets b narrowed to local 192.0.2.0/24 do the same. They enforce Ze's stricter stated rule (a pair is operator-fixed only when it is the whole configured policy, and a tunnel only by a configured selector), not the Section 5.1 MUST, and the rfc/short Support remaining text claims (b) and (c) (narrowed "on either half") with no test that proves the local half beyond protocol. Not counted, no 5.1 effect: respondChildRekey judging narrowing in decidedChildMode instead of old.Mode stays green because the install claim refuses what narrowing passes.
